products.overview: A reactor, a pipeline, or a conveyor belt isn't a place for a delicate instrument. It's dusty, it swings in temperature, and it's often somewhere the safety rules don't let a standard analyzer sit at all. MATRIX-F II solves that with distance: the spectrometer sits in a protected analysis house, and an industry-hardened fiber optic probe reaches into the process itself, with no measurement delay. It's the only FT-NIR spectrometer that measures both in contact and contactless with one instrument, using fiber optic probes for direct immersion and fiber-coupled heads with tungsten sources for contactless measurement from a distance, up to six connected at once. Ten years of warranty cover the interferometer and the solid-state laser, and Bruker states thousands of these are already installed across chemical, pharmaceutical, and food manufacturing.

faqs.question: What is the MATRIX-F II FT-NIR Process Spectrometer used for?
faqs.answer: MATRIX-F II is used for direct, real-time monitoring of chemical processes in reactors, pipelines, and conveyor belts, across chemical, pharmaceutical, and food manufacturing.

faqs.question: What makes MATRIX-F II different from a standard FT-NIR spectrometer?
faqs.answer: It's the only FT-NIR spectrometer that measures both in contact and contactless with one instrument, using fiber optic probes for direct measurement and fiber-coupled heads for remote measurement.

faqs.question: How do I choose between contact and contactless measurement for my process?
faqs.answer: Use a fiber optic probe wherever direct immersion into the process is possible, and a contactless head where physical contact isn't practical, such as a moving conveyor belt or web; the duplex variant supports both at once.

faqs.question: How do I set up monitoring for multiple points on one production line?
faqs.answer: Connect up to six contactless heads to a single MATRIX-F II emission or duplex spectrometer, allowing simultaneous monitoring across multiple points from one instrument.

faqs.question: Can MATRIX-F II be installed in a hazardous or ATEX-classified area?
faqs.answer: Yes, using the MATRIX-F exproof variant, certified to II 2G Ex px II T6 Gb and II (1) G [Ex op is T4 Ga] II C standards.

faqs.question: Can a method developed in the lab be used directly in the process?
faqs.answer: Yes. MATRIX-F II can run as a stand-alone laboratory system during method development, then transfer directly into the process application without redevelopment.

faqs.question: What is the warranty on the MATRIX-F II?
faqs.answer: 10 years on the interferometer's moving parts and the solid-state laser.

faqs.question: Is MATRIX-F II suitable for pharmaceutical manufacturing?
faqs.answer: Yes. An automated filter wheel and the OPUS Validation Program confirm the instrument operates within specification, which Bruker states is the precondition for pharmaceutical applications.

faqs.question: How does MATRIX-F II connect to existing plant control systems?
faqs.answer: Through CMET software with an OPC interface, supporting standard protocols including 4-20mA, Modbus, and Profibus DP.

faqs.answer: The price depends on the variant, probes, and housing your installation needs. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your process requirements are confirmed.

sections.eyebrow: Fiber Optic Probes and Contactless Measurement
sections.title: Fiber Optic Probes and Contactless Measurement
body: Choosing between contact and contactless measurement, or using both, comes down to what your process point actually allows.

Fiber optic probes go into the process directly, as diffuse reflectance, transflectance, or transmission probes, in materials like stainless steel or Hastelloy, or as flow cells for pilot plant assemblies. Contactless heads use tungsten illumination to measure from a distance, with the scattered light carried back to the spectrometer by fiber, useful where physical contact with the process isn't practical or safe. The duplex variant runs both at once, so a single instrument covers a reactor immersion probe and a remote conveyor head simultaneously.

faqs.question: What is the MATRIX-MF FT-IR Process Reaction Monitoring solution used for?
faqs.answer: MATRIX-MF monitors chemical and biological reactions in real time, using a direct-contact diamond ATR probe placed in the reaction itself, in the lab or on a process line.

faqs.question: How is MATRIX-MF different from MATRIX-F II?
faqs.answer: MATRIX-MF works the mid-IR region using direct-contact ATR probes, while MATRIX-F II works the near-IR region using fiber optic probes and contactless heads. They suit different measurement needs and are sometimes used together.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right ATR probe for my reaction?
faqs.answer: Match the probe diameter to your vessel scale: IN351 (3.17 mm) for micro-scale reactions, IN355 (6.3 mm) for standard lab vessels, or IN350-T (6 mm) and IN356-EX (12 mm) where ATEX hazardous-area compliance is required.

faqs.question: How do I monitor several reactions at once with MATRIX-MF?
faqs.answer: Connect up to six probes to the built-in automated multiplexer, allowing one instrument to monitor up to six reactions simultaneously.

faqs.question: Can MATRIX-MF be used in a hazardous, ATEX-classified area?
faqs.answer: Yes, either using the IN350-T or IN356-EX ATEX-rated probes, or the fully certified MATRIX-MF exproof variant.

faqs.question: Can MATRIX-MF monitor biological reactions, not just chemical ones?
faqs.answer: Yes. Mid-IR ATR sampling suits biological process monitoring as well as chemical reaction monitoring.

faqs.question: How quickly can probes be swapped on the MATRIX-MF?
faqs.answer: Bruker's proprietary BQC quick-connector design allows fast probe exchange in seconds, without compromising measurement reproducibility.

faqs.question: Can MATRIX-MF move between the lab and the production line?
faqs.answer: Yes. Its small footprint works as a standalone lab system, or mounts in a standard 19-inch rack for process installation.

faqs.question: How is MATRIX-MF validated for regulated use?
faqs.answer: The OPUS Validation Program runs automated performance tests through a built-in filter wheel, tracking hardware and consumable status continuously.

faqs.answer: The price depends on the probe selection, multiplexer configuration, and hazard rating your installation needs. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

body: The right probe is the one whose diameter and rating actually match your reaction vessel and environment.

The IN351 Micro ATR probe, at 3.17 mm, suits small-volume or micro-scale reactions where a larger probe simply won't fit. The IN355, at 6.3 mm, covers general lab-scale reaction vessels. Where the installation needs ATEX compliance, the IN350-T (6 mm) and IN356-EX (12 mm) are both rated for hazardous areas, with the larger IN356-EX suited to bigger process lines. All four connect through the same BQC quick-connector, so switching between them mid-project doesn't mean re-learning the setup.

longForm.heroHook: A diamond probe, directly in the reaction. Watching it happen, live.
heroParagraphs: Some measurements need distance. This one needs direct contact.
MATRIX-MF puts a diamond ATR probe right into the reaction mixture, in the lab or on the process line, and reads the mid-infrared region that carries the richest chemical information available.

Four named probe options cover everything from a 3.17 mm micro-scale reaction to a 12 mm process line, two of them rated for ATEX hazardous areas. Bruker's quick-connector design swaps probes in seconds, without compromising reproducibility.

One instrument monitors up to six reactions simultaneously through its built-in multiplexer. The optics sit sealed against the environment, on the same RockSolid interferometer and DigiTect electronics used across Bruker's research-grade spectrometers.

faqs.question: What is the BEAM Process FT-NIR Spectrometer used for?
faqs.answer: BEAM monitors solid and semi-solid material in real time, mounted directly on pipelines, hoppers, or conveyor belts, across food, feed, polymer, and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

faqs.question: What makes BEAM different from a conventional single-point NIR analyzer?
faqs.answer: It's the first dedicated single-point spectrometer to carry the full spectral range and resolution of FT-NIR spectroscopy, handling applications conventional single-point analyzers can't reach.

faqs.question: How fast does BEAM measure?
faqs.answer: More than 250 scans per minute, fast enough to catch process variation as it happens.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right mounting hardware for my installation?
faqs.answer: Use Tri-Clamp flanges for hygienic pipeline or sight-glass connections, mounting brackets for flexible orientation on conveyors or hoppers, and the laboratory stand for method development before transferring to production.

faqs.question: How do I keep monitoring running if a light source fails?
faqs.answer: Dual source mode switches automatically to a backup light source when the primary fails, so measurement continues without waiting for a service visit.

faqs.question: Can I develop a method in the lab before installing BEAM on the line?
faqs.answer: Yes. The laboratory stand provides the correct measurement distance using a Petri dish turntable or the supplied holder, so a method developed in the lab transfers directly to production.

faqs.question: What feed parameters can BEAM measure?
faqs.answer: Moisture, oil, protein, fiber, and ash, plus more specialized parameters including ADF, NDF, and amino acids, in both raw materials and finished feed.

faqs.question: Is BEAM suitable for pharmaceutical process monitoring?
faqs.answer: Yes. Typical applications include monitoring mixing processes and determining the endpoint of API drying.

faqs.question: What is dual source mode?
faqs.answer: A redundancy feature that automatically switches to a second light source if the primary one fails, doubling system availability and avoiding unplanned downtime.

faqs.question: What is the price of the BEAM Process FT-NIR Spectrometer in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on the mounting hardware and configuration your installation needs. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Bruker BEAM Process FT-NIR Spectrometer in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

sections.tabSummary: What over-250-scans-a-minute and dual source actually buy you
body: Two things make BEAM viable for continuous process use where other single-point analyzers fall short: it doesn't compromise on spectral performance, and it doesn't go dark when one component fails.

The full NIR spectral range is normally the domain of larger FT-NIR systems, not dedicated single-point analyzers, which is what lets BEAM handle applications conventional single-point instruments can't reach. At over 250 scans a minute, that performance runs fast enough to track a moving process rather than sample it after the fact. And dual source mode means a failed light source doesn't mean a stopped line: the system switches to its backup automatically.
